fatal_errors: The proposed Ni-based superalloy/HEA system does not identify the studied FCC/BCC Al-Cr-Fe-Ni multilayer, particularly the 16 nm modulation-period material.
The proposed elevated-temperature regime conflicts with the room-temperature nanoindentation-creep conditions of the target study.

The coherency–mechanism relationship is substantially reversed: the target attributes diffusion/interface-slip behavior to semicoherent interfaces with misfit-dislocation pileup and possible amorphization, whereas coherent interfaces permit more dislocation-mediated deformation.
The baseline of single-phase Ni alloys does not match the coherent M8 and grain-boundary-dominated M32/M80 multilayer controls.
No evidence is cited for the asserted Ni-based material or mechanism.
explanation: The hypothesis recognizes that interface coherency and layer thickness can control a transition between diffusion- and dislocation-mediated creep, and its proposed coherency series with creep and TEM measurements is testable. However, it misses the specific Al-Cr-Fe-Ni FCC/BCC multilayer and the critical 16 nm semicoherent architecture. It also substitutes high-temperature bulk-style creep for room-temperature nanoindentation and proposes the opposite mechanistic role for coherent versus semicoherent interfaces. The experiment could test a plausible generic alternative, but the material claim and mechanism lack supporting evidence and do not reconstruct the reported result.
